messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@lumen.ai>, Carlos Mendes <carlos@lumen.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Escape velocity: Q4 capacity plan to avoid throttling at renewal

Hi Samira / Carlos,

Congrats on a strong quarter — saw the traffic spikes in your public dashboard. With your renewal coming up and the recent throughput growth, I want to make sure we avoid the throttling hit you saw in September. Can you send the last 60 days of GPU utilization by hour (even a CSV is fine)?

High-level ask from our side:
- peak sustained utilization windows (1h, 4h)
- percent of requests that need <250ms tail latency
- any expected product launches between now and Feb

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min capacity sync today or tomorrow to walk through a prescriptive plan — we usually produce a stepped commit + burst handoff that covers thermal/maintenance margins.

Thanks,
Avery

Sure — attaching a trimmed export. Quick summary:
- 60-day peak: sustained 82% average utilization across your dedicated pool during 10:00–14:00 PST (weekday business hours).
- Short spikes up to 98% for 10–20 minute bursts during model training campaigns.
- ~68% of inference calls require sub-250ms tail latency (we measure this at the gateway).
- Planned product launches: small feature rollout in mid-December; larger cross-region beta slated for Feb.

We attached: lumen_usage_q3_snapshot.csv (hourly utilization + latency buckets).

We'd like a recommended sizing that avoids the 95th percentile throttles but keeps cost sensible — procurement starts internal approvals next week.

Thanks,
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, LumenAI
samira@lumen.ai

Attachment: lumen_usage_q3_snapshot.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@lumen.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Escape velocity: Q4 capacity plan to avoid throttling at renewal

Thanks for the export, Samira — helpful dataset. I pulled peak-window aggregates and sketched a 3-step prescriptive plan to balance cost, latency, and safety margin.

(analysis) Key signals from CSV:
- Weekday business hours drive the bulk of sustained load; 4hr window median at 78% utilization, 95th at 92%.
- Burst behavior: short 10–20m spikes to 95–98% that correlate with scheduled retrains.
- Latency SLOs: ~68% must be sub-250ms, but the remaining tail tolerates up to 1s for non-frontend requests.

Recommended playbook (Escape Velocity plan):
1) Immediate (0–30 days): add a 16-GPU reserved tranche (H100 equivalent) to raise baseline dedicated capacity from 64 -> 80 GPUs. This reduces sustained utilization 78% -> ~63% and lowers tail pressure.
2) Near-term (30–90 days): convert an existing 24-GPU burst pool into a hybrid 12-burst + 12-reserved slice. This improves predictable throughput for weekday peaks while preserving burst headroom for retrains.
3) Safety & ops: reserve a 6% thermal/maintenance buffer (equivalent to ~5 GPUs) and enable automatic fallback routing to a compatible quantized model during 95%+ short spikes.

Estimated commercial impact: incremental committed monthly spend approx $43k (USD) for the 16-GPU tranche (list-equivalent pricing), with a projected reduction in throttling incidents of ~85% during peak windows. I attached a one-page playbook and a CSV-derived summary.

Next steps I suggest:
- Confirm procurement runway (Samira: you said approvals next week?)
- Technical sync (30 min) with your infra team to agree throttle thresholds and fallback model mix — available slots Mon/Tue next week.
- If approved, I'll draft an amendment for the 16-GPU tranche + hybrid conversion term sheet.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0199

Attachment: escape_velocity_capacity_playbook.pdf (1 page, proposal)

--
